title: Reported Speech Relay
intro: “I’m tired” becomes “she said she was tired”. Practise how verbs move back when you report what someone said.

A2.q: Direct: "I am tired." Reported: She said she ___ tired.
A2.why: “Am” moves back to “was” in reported speech, and “she” takes “was”.

A2.q: Direct: "I like pizza." Reported: He said he ___ pizza.
A2.why: After “said”, present simple usually moves back to past simple: “liked”.

A2.q: Direct: "I have a car." Reported: She said she ___ a car.
A2.why: “Have” (own) moves back to “had”; it is not used in the continuous here.

A2.q: Direct: "I can swim." Reported: He said he ___ swim.
A2.why: “Can” moves back to “could”, followed by the verb with no “to”.

A2.q: Direct: "I will call you." Reported: She said she ___ call me.
A2.why: “Will” moves back to “would”, followed by the verb with no “to”.

A2.q: Direct: "I am working." Reported: He said he ___ working.
A2.why: “Am working” moves back to “was working”; “she/he” takes “was”.

A2.q: Direct: "I don't know." Reported: She said she ___ know.
A2.why: “Don’t know” moves back to “didn’t know”: the helper “did” does the work.

A2.q: Direct: "I want to go." Reported: He said he ___ to go.
A2.why: Present simple “want” moves back to past simple “wanted”.

A2.q: Direct: "I live in Madrid." Reported: She said she ___ in Madrid.
A2.why: After “said”, present simple usually moves back: “lived” (if it is still true, “lives” is also possible).

A2.q: Direct: "I need help." Reported: He said he ___ help.
A2.why: Present simple “need” moves back to past simple “needed”.

A2.q: Direct: "I love my horse." Reported: The cowboy said he loved ___ horse.
A2.why: In reported speech “my” changes to match the speaker: the cowboy’s horse is “his”.

A2.q: Direct: "We are from Valencia." Reported: They said ___ were from Valencia.
A2.why: “We” becomes “they” when someone else reports it; “them” cannot be a subject.

B1.q: Direct: "I saw her yesterday." Reported: He said he ___ her the day before.
B1.why: “Saw” moves back to past perfect “had seen”; “the day before” replaces “yesterday”.

B1.q: Direct: "I'll finish it tomorrow." Reported: She said she ___ finish it the next day.
B1.why: “The next day” shows the report comes later, so “will” moves back to “would”.

B1.q: Direct: "I bought this here." Reported: He said he ___ it there.
B1.why: “Bought” moves back to past perfect, and the participle is “bought”, not “buy”.

B1.q: Direct: "We are leaving now." Reported: They said they ___ leaving then.
B1.why: “Are leaving” moves back to “were leaving”, and “now” becomes “then”.

B1.q: Direct: "I have finished my homework." Reported: She said she ___ finished her homework.
B1.why: Present perfect “have finished” moves back to past perfect “had finished”.

B1.q: Direct: "I went there last week." Reported: He said he ___ there the week before.
B1.why: “Went” moves back to “had gone”; the participle is “gone”, never “went”.

B1.q: Direct: "I must leave soon." Reported: She said she ___ leave soon.
B1.why: “Must” for an obligation is usually reported as “had to”; “must” never takes “to”.

B1.q: Direct: "This is my book." Reported: He said ___ was his book.
B1.why: “This” becomes “that” when you report from a distance in time or place.

B1.q: Direct: "I'll see you tomorrow." Reported: She said she would see me the ___ day.
B1.why: “Tomorrow” becomes “the next day” in reported speech.

B1.q: Direct: "I came here yesterday." Reported: He said he ___ come there the day before.
B1.why: “Came” moves back to past perfect: “had come”, and “here” becomes “there”.

B1.q: Direct: "I wrote the letter last night." Reported: She said she had written the letter the ___ night.
B1.why: “Last night” becomes “the previous night” when you report it later.

B1.q: Direct: "I can't come to the fiesta." Reported: He said he ___ come to the fiesta.
B1.why: “Can’t” moves back to “couldn’t”, with no “to” and no “did”.

B2.q: Direct: "Where do you live?" Reported: She asked me where I ___.
B2.why: A reported question uses statement order and the past: “where I lived”, no “do”.

B2.q: Direct: "Can you help me?" Reported: He asked if I ___ help him.
B2.why: “Can” moves back to “could” in the reported question; no “to” after it.

B2.q: Direct: "Close the door." Reported: She told me ___ the door.
B2.why: An order is reported with “told me” + “to” + verb.

B2.q: Direct: "Don't touch that." Reported: He told me ___ touch that.
B2.why: A negative order is “told me not to” + verb.

B2.q: Direct: "What time is it?" Reported: She asked what time ___.
B2.why: Reported questions use statement order and move back: “what time it was”.

B2.q: Direct: "Have you finished?" Reported: He asked if I ___ finished.
B2.why: Present perfect moves back to past perfect: “if I had finished”.

B2.q: Direct: "I may be late." Reported: She said she ___ be late.
B2.why: “May” for a possibility is reported as “might”, with no “to” after it.

B2.q: Direct: "Are you coming?" Reported: He asked if I ___ coming.
B2.why: “Are you coming?” becomes “if I was coming”: statement order and past tense.

B2.q: Direct: "Please wait here." Reported: She asked me ___ wait there.
B2.why: A polite request is reported with “asked me to” + verb.

B2.q: Direct: "Why are you crying?" Reported: He asked me why I ___ crying.
B2.why: “Are you crying” moves back to “I was crying”, in statement order.

B2.q: Direct: "Did you see the outlaws?" Reported: The sheriff asked if I ___ the outlaws.
B2.why: “Did you see” becomes “if I had seen”: no “did”, statement order, past perfect.

B2.q: Direct: "Don't drink the water from that pump." Reported: John Snow warned people ___ the water from that pump.
B2.why: A warning is reported with “warned” + person + “not to” + verb.

C1.q: Direct: "The Earth orbits the Sun." Reported: The teacher explained that the Earth ___ the Sun.
C1.why: A fact that is always true can stay in the present: the Earth still orbits the Sun.

C1.q: Direct: "I'll help if I can." Reported: She promised she ___ help if she could.
C1.why: “Promised” + “if she could” shows the shift back: “will” becomes “would”.

C1.q: Direct: "I broke the vase." Reported: He admitted ___ the vase.
C1.why: “Admit” is followed by the “-ing” form: “admitted breaking”.

C1.q: Direct: "You should see a doctor." Reported: She advised me ___ a doctor.
Direct: "I won't do it again." Reported: He promised ___ do it again.
C1.why: “Promise not to” + verb is the negative pattern; “not” goes before “to”.

C1.q: Direct: "It was my fault." Reported: She admitted that it ___ her fault.
C1.why: “Was” is moved back a step to past perfect after “admitted”: “had been”.

C1.q: Direct: "Let's go to the cinema." Reported: He suggested ___ to the cinema.
C1.why: “Suggest” is followed by the “-ing” form: “suggested going”.

C1.q: Direct: "I'm sorry I lied." Reported: She apologised for ___.
C1.why: “Apologise for” + “-ing”: after a preposition the verb takes “-ing”.

C1.q: Direct: "You must apply by Friday." Reported: They informed us that we ___ apply by Friday.
C1.why: An obligation with “must” is reported as “had to”; “must” never takes “to”.

C1.q: Direct: "I didn't take the money." Reported: He denied ___ the money.
C1.why: “Deny” is followed by the “-ing” form: “denied taking”.

C1.q: Direct: "You stole my horse!" Reported: The rancher accused him ___ his horse.
Direct: "Wash your hands before you examine a patient." Reported: Semmelweis insisted ___ doctors wash their hands before examining patients.
C1.why: “Insist that” + person + base verb: “insisted that doctors wash”.
